title: The Drifting Classroom
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Kazuo Umezu's 1972-74 horror classic sends an entire elementary school into a polluted, post-apocalyptic future. The adults go mad or are killed, and sixth grader Sho tries to lead the children through monsters, plague, famine and revolt, while his mother in the present helps him across time (Wikipedia; ANN; Viz blurb via MangaUpdates).
life_message: Refusing to sacrifice anyone, and holding on to love and hope, is what keeps people human when the world collapses.

content.note: A teacher murders colleagues and pupils, a man burns teachers alive, children die to monsters and floods (Wikipedia; ANN); AniList Gore 84; Viz rated 18+ (ANN).
Relentless horror, madness and child deaths; ANN calls it 'harrowing' (ANN; Wikipedia; AniList Survival/Tragedy).
Mild crushes only (Wikipedia); ANN notes dated 'casually sexist' remarks.
Adults descend into insanity; ANN mentions children jumping from the roof (ANN; Wikipedia).
Surgery without anesthetic and child armed revolt (ANN; Wikipedia).

dominant: Survival without adults; pollution's future; idealism against brutality

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Disputes become armed revolt, but Sho seeks order and reconciliation (Wikipedia).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Children form a quasi-government, 'Nation of Yamato Elementary', to survive (Wikipedia).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Mother-son bond drives rescue; Sho protects every child equally.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Adult authority collapses; children choose leaders (Wikipedia; ANN).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Science and planning save them; a deified mother bust shows ritual's pull (ANN).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Food, water and plague dominate every arc (Wikipedia; MU Survival).

folkways.japan: The school as a self-governing class with representatives and a strong pull toward group unity reflects Japanese school culture of the 1970s.

delivery.evidence: ANN: message comes through events and dilemmas, though Sho 'repeatedly argues for goodness'; adults shown as weak or monstrous.
delivery.note: Selfish adult survivalism appears only through a mad, sadistic man, while the pragmatist classmate is given honor and a confession.

winners_losers: Children who keep compassion and cooperation survive and vow to rebuild; violent adults and hoarders die. Sympathy goes to childhood idealism and the mother's love.
